Methods for SEMFit objects

Source: R/methods-sem.R
SEMFit-methods.Rd

Accessors and display for a SEMFit returned by fit_sem().

Arguments

object, x

A SEMFit object

...

Additional arguments (ignored)

Value

coef() a named numeric vector; vcov() a matrix; nobs() an integer; logLik() an object of class "logLik"; summary() an object of class "summary_SEMFit"; print() invisibly returns its argument.

Details

  • coef() returns the free-parameter estimates, named as lavaan names its coefficients: the label when the row has one, else lhs op rhs without spaces ("M~X", "X~~X", "eta=~m2"). vcov(), tidy() and the accessors extract_mediation() reads use the same names.

  • vcov() returns their covariance, projected onto the active constraints and bounds; rows for a pinned parameter are zero.

  • nobs() returns the number of rows used after listwise deletion.

  • logLik() returns the log likelihood with the means free; its df attribute counts the free parameters plus one mean per observed variable that is not fixed. With fixed_x it is conditional on the fixed variables (lavaan's value), so AIC() and BIC() of fits with different fixed sets or data stop instead of ranking them; the same holds for anova() and mbco_sem(). A fixed_x fit also lists its fixed moments after the free parameters in tidy() (fixed_x column TRUE, no standard error) and in summary(); coef() and vcov() leave them out. print() and summary() say what the log likelihood is conditional on.

  • Model test with a product term. The global chi-square is not valid when a factor of a product term (x:m) is itself a regression target, because the model then treats the product as exogenous although it is a function of m; nor when the variances and covariances of the exogenous variables (every product included) are restricted (fixed, labeled, bounded, or left out because a ~~ statement names one of them; a fixed_x moment is not a restriction). fit_sem() then warns once, glance() reports chisq, df and p_value as NA (with the reason in attr(, "note")), summary() prints the reason, and anova() and mbco_sem() stop naming the product. The coefficients equal equation-wise least squares and the sandwich standard errors are unaffected, but only with observed information: fit_sem(information = "expected") stops for a product with an endogenous factor, because its standard errors (the sandwich built on them included) are wrong there. fit_sem() also warns once for any product term fitted without se_type = "sandwich". logLik(), AIC() and BIC() stay defined, but the values of a fit with a product are not comparable with those of a fit without one (the product column enters the likelihood), so AIC(fit_a, fit_b), BIC(), anova() and mbco_sem() refuse such a pair.

  • anova() tests nested fits by the likelihood-ratio statistic \(n (F_r - F_f)\) on the difference in model degrees of freedom: anova(fit_full, fit_restricted), or several fits, each tested against the one with fewer degrees of freedom. It compares fits that were already made and never refits. The fits must use the same observed variables and rows, and neither may have sampling weights or have failed to converge. Nesting is checked by parameter-table inclusion: the restricted fit may free no parameter the other leaves out and must have more degrees of freedom. That is necessary for nesting, not sufficient; whether two models are nested in substance is the analyst's responsibility. A restricted fit with a smaller discrepancy than the model it restricts is an error (one fit is not at its global optimum). When a bound or an inequality on a tested parameter is active at the restricted fit, the null lies on the boundary of the parameter space, the statistic is a mixture of chi-squares, and the function warns that the p-value is not valid, as mbco_sem() does. Returns an object of class "anova" with columns Df, Chisq (n times the discrepancy), Chisq diff, Df diff and Pr(>Chisq). Name rows by naming the arguments after the first.

  • confint() returns Wald (normal) intervals for the free parameters and the defined parameters, confint(fit, parm, level = 0.95); parm takes names or positions. A parameter pinned by a constraint or sitting on a bound has a zero standard error and a point interval.

  • tidy() returns one row per free parameter, then the moments fixed_x fixed (a fixed_x column, only when something is fixed), then per defined parameter: term (the name coef() uses), op (the operator of its row in the parameter table, := for a defined parameter), estimate, std_error, statistic (the z value, NA when the standard error is zero), p_value (two-sided), and with conf_int = TRUE the interval confint() returns (conf_low, conf_high, at conf_level). type is "all" (default), "parameters" or "defined".

  • glance() returns one row: nobs, npar (free parameters after the equality constraints), df, chisq (n times the minimized discrepancy, the test of the model against the saturated one), p_value (NA when df is 0), logLik, AIC and BIC (with the means free, as logLik() defines them) and fixed_x, the names the fit holds at their sample moments, comma-joined ("" when none). A fit with sampling weights has no likelihood, so its chisq, p_value, logLik, AIC and BIC are NA. There is no converged column: fit_sem() returns a fit only for a solution that passed the acceptance gate and errors otherwise, so @converged is TRUE for every SEMFit and would carry no information.

  • summary() collects the estimates, standard errors and z statistics, the defined parameters, and the diagnostics: rows dropped, information type, degrees of freedom, retries, stationarity, active bounds and constraints, improper-solution flags and the multiplier sign check.

See also

fit_sem(), SEMFit

Examples

# \donttest{
fit <- fit_sem(
  "mediator1 ~ a*treatment\noutcome ~ b*mediator1 + treatment\nab := a*b",
  data = mediation_demo
)
coef(fit)
#>                    a                    b    outcome~treatment 
#>           0.45599612           0.71342873           0.04057666 
#> mediator1~~mediator1     outcome~~outcome treatment~~treatment 
#>           1.15847022           1.18044624           0.24999375 
vcov(fit)[c("a", "b"), c("a", "b")]
#>               a             b
#> a  1.158499e-02 -3.349652e-14
#> b -3.349652e-14  2.547425e-03
nobs(fit)
#> [1] 400
summary(fit)
#> Summary of SEMFit
#> =================
#> 
#> Observations: 400
#> Degrees of freedom: 0
#> Information: observed
#> Standard errors: model-based
#> Converged: Yes
#> 
#> Parameters:
#>                    name    est     se       z      p
#>                       a 0.4560 0.1076  4.2366 <1e-04
#>                       b 0.7134 0.0505 14.1351 <1e-04
#>     outcome ~ treatment 0.0406 0.1111  0.3654  0.715
#>  mediator1 ~~ mediator1 1.1585 0.0819 14.1421 <1e-04
#>      outcome ~~ outcome 1.1804 0.0835 14.1421 <1e-04
#>  treatment ~~ treatment 0.2500 0.0177 14.1421 <1e-04
#> 
#> Defined parameters:
#>  name expr    est     se
#>    ab  a*b 0.3253 0.0802
#> 
#> Diagnostics:
#>   Optimizer status: 4; stationarity 1.22e-08; retries 0
#>   Active bounds: none
#>   Active constraints: none
#>   Improper solution: no
#>   Multiplier sign check: ok
generics::tidy(fit, conf_int = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 7 × 8
#>   term            op    estimate std_error statistic  p_value conf_low conf_high
#>   <chr>           <chr>    <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 a               ~       0.456     0.108      4.24  2.27e- 5    0.245     0.667
#> 2 b               ~       0.713     0.0505    14.1   2.31e-45    0.615     0.812
#> 3 outcome~treatm… ~       0.0406    0.111      0.365 7.15e- 1   -0.177     0.258
#> 4 mediator1~~med… ~~      1.16      0.0819    14.1   2.09e-45    0.998     1.32 
#> 5 outcome~~outco… ~~      1.18      0.0835    14.1   2.09e-45    1.02      1.34 
#> 6 treatment~~tre… ~~      0.250     0.0177    14.1   2.09e-45    0.215     0.285
#> 7 ab              :=      0.325     0.0802     4.06  4.95e- 5    0.168     0.482
generics::glance(fit)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 9
#>    nobs  npar    df chisq p_value logLik   AIC   BIC fixed_x
#>   <int> <int> <dbl> <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <chr>  
#> 1   400     6     0     0      NA -1488. 2994. 3030. ""     

# a likelihood-ratio test of b = 0 against the fitted model
fit0 <- fit_sem(paste0(fit@model, "\nb == 0"), data = mediation_demo)
anova(fit, fit0)
#> Likelihood-ratio (chi-square difference) test for SEMFit models
#> 
#> n = 400; Chisq is n times the minimized discrepancy
#> 
#>      Df  Chisq Chisq diff Df diff Pr(>Chisq)    
#> fit   0   0.00                                  
#> fit0  1 162.05     162.05       1  < 2.2e-16 ***
#> ---
#> Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1
# }
